title: Black Hole Recordings New Releases – Week 43
excerpt: Find the latest electronic music news, features, interviews, videos and podcasts from Beatportal - the reference for DJs and dance music artists.
content:
A selection of this week’s standout releases across the dancefloor.

One release takes us into the final hours of a sunrise-chasing journey, another turns a trance classic into an emotional peak-time moment, while acid lines and melodic breaks set the course for a different kind of intensity. From the nostalgia that first draws us to trance to a patient, two-year creation and the fleeting connections made on a night out, this week is full of stories that unfold long after the beat drops.

Markus Schulz – In Search Of Sunrise 22

With Nocturnal Voyage, Markus Schulz takes the third and final chapter of In Search Of Sunrise 22 into darker territory, pushing the series towards a late-night, techno-leaning sound. Hypnotic grooves and slow-building tension replace big melodic peaks, while preserving the emotional core of ISOS.

Alongside new Dakota material and fresh aliases Aeridan and Shadow Assembly, Schulz introduces emerging names including Elias Erium, Hobin Rude & N-TCHBL, and Enlusion, while welcoming progressive house icon Guy J to the series for the first time. Reworks of established trance favourites carry the mix towards its last phase, with Markus Schulz & BLR revisiting “The Silmarillia” before BT’s “If Memory Serves (Lunar Mode)” brings the trilogy to a close.

Mark Sherry & Sarah Howells – Heroes (Craig Connelly Remix)

Craig Connelly reimagines “Heroes,” shifting the emphasis from pure drive to the emotion beneath it. The pace remains relentless, but the melodies carry a different weight, giving Sarah Howells’ vocals more room to connect. Rather than easing off, Connelly builds on the intensity, allowing tension and uplift to work hand in hand. The result keeps the momentum high while drawing listeners deeper into the song’s narrative, proving that a remix can hit just as hard emotionally as it does on the dancefloor.

Sylvie Miles – The Script

At 145 BPM, “The Script” sees Sylvie Miles balance raw peak-time intensity with a more personal, melodic touch. An emotional breakdown gives way to sharp acid synths, restoring the tension and creating a striking contrast between reflection and release.

The idea behind the title is about trusting our own life’s script. Even when something doesn’t feel right or make sense at first, I believe there can still be a purpose behind it.

- Sylvie Miles

That philosophy carries through the arrangement, with the melodies offering a moment of calm before the acid takes over, turning an introspective message into a powerful club moment.

Baedine – Neophoria

Every new trance producer starts somewhere, and for Baedine, it begins with the sound that first drew him to the genre. “Neophoria” revisits the bright melodies and uplifting spirit of classic trance, adding a contemporary edge as he starts to establish his own identity. Its title captures the space between nostalgia and progress: holding on to the feeling that sparked his love for trance while remaining open to where it might lead next.

Plastic Boy – Silver Bath (Charles D Remix)

Some melodies stay with you long after you’ve forgotten where you first heard them. For Charles D, that feeling inspired his rework of “Silver Bath,” originally released under Mike Push’s Plastic Boy alias, after the two connected in 2025 through their shared appreciation for high-impact electronic music.

Preserving the emotional core of the original, Charles D adds his signature peak-time techno drive, bridging classic trance sentiment with modern club power. Initially intended for vinyl only, the remix has since featured in Mike Push’s sets at Tomorrowland, with support from Markus Schulz, bringing a familiar classic to a new generation.

I'm happy that ‘Silver Bath’ is still reaching new generations and that people continue to connect with it after all these years, and good remixes are the next evolution.

- Mike Push

Eco – Cloud People

Sitting between progressive house and trance, “Cloud People” finds Eco exploring the space where neither genre needs to dominate. Two years in the making, the composition unfolds patiently through live guitar, synths, keys, vocals and carefully layered atmospheres, rising and falling without rushing towards a predictable climax.

A nostalgic thread runs throughout, recalling the deeper side of progressive trance through references such as Salt Tank’s “Eugina” (Michael Woods Remix) and Gabriel & Dresden’s mix of Sarah McLachlan’s “Fallen.” Rather than simply revisiting those influences, Eco uses them as a foundation for something open-ended, familiar yet full of possibility.

CYRUS – Club Crush

“Club Crush” captures the fleeting connection that can happen on a night out: locking eyes with a stranger, spending hours together on the dancefloor and feeling as though you’ve known each other for much longer. CYRUS channels that experience through a groovy, tech-influenced house arrangement, with filtered female vocals adding an air of mystery. The atmosphere shifts between romance and melancholy, while a breakbeat switch disrupts the groove, mirroring the emotional highs and lows of the encounter. Then the night ends, the music stops, and you realise you never asked for their number, leaving only the hope of crossing paths again next weekend.
